title.narrative: BResilient - Bamboo as a vital ingredient in reforestation strategies to promote resilient and sustainable communities and enterprises in Madagascar

description.narrative: Improving climate resilience of peri-urban communities and forests in coastal Madagascar through the sustainable management and utilization of bamboo plantations, reforestation of natural forest, and development of a local economy that fosters sustainable livelihoods and the responsible sourcing of timber and bamboo.

The programme has three outcomes: 1. Reforestation strategies designed to support biodiversity conservation and adapted to meet community needsSustainable management and utilization of 32 hectares of bamboo plantations and 14 hectares of natural forest. The project case studies will provide information on forest ecosystems, species present, and ecological processes. Identifying suitable species and plantation strategies for reforestation in these locations will restore damaged ecosystems and conserve endangered species. Training local communities, NGOs, and government organisations in forest management and stewardship promotes successful and enduring reforestation via an increase in respect for forest ecosystems, via encouraging cultivation, and providing alternative solutions for resource demands and enterprises.2. Sustainable resource use adapted to local needs, strengthening resilience to climate changeImproved climate resilience and access to sustainable fuel and construction materials for 6,000 community members. Improving people’s resilience whilst reducing their dependency on dwindling forest resources lies at the heart of this proposal. We will work with communities to understand their specific resource demands and ability to adapt to using a new resource. We will teach community, NGO, and government representatives how to design and build resilient bamboo structures and how to adapt bamboo for fuel use (charcoal), to suit their environment, culture, and available resources.3. Establishment and strengthening of enterprises focused on bamboo-related activitiesImproved livelihoods for case study communities, establishment and strengthening of 32 enterprise clusters. Introducing bamboo into reforestation strategies will provide a new forest product for sustainable enterprises. We will train local community members in entrepreneurship and enterprise creation. The training targets young people, as those who will establish new long-term enterprises, and women, to address gender inequality in economic opportunities [22]. Communities will directly benefit from enterprise opportunities arising from alternative materials (e.g. producing and selling bamboo charcoal) and indirectly through improved resilience.

The programme will operate in two coastal regions of Madagascar: Analanjirofo (district of Fénérive Est) and Boeny (district of Mahajanga). Both regions are particularly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, facing annual cyclones, that make them ideal for testing climate resilience and material adaptability in Madagascar’s unique environmental context. The Fénérive Est district has a humid climate, where bamboo is only minimally used, supporting efforts to enhance bamboo’s role in climate-resilient construction and sustainable reforestation. In contrast, Mahajanga district is a dry ecosystem, and where bamboo is less utilized, providing a contrasting environment to explore bamboo's adaptability and viability in drier, less forested areas. Mahajanga is more populated than Fénérive Est, representing a contrast in terms of both urbanization and infrastructure. The distinct ecological conditions and size of these districts are representative Madagascar’s coastal zones broadly, supporting the scalability of programme results. Activities will focus on five communes: Ambodimanga II, Ampasimbe Manantsatrana, and Ampasina Maningory in Fénérive Est, and Boanamary, Belobaka, in Mahajanga. These locations are chosen for their forest resources and peri-urban characteristics, on which the livelihoods of 100,000 people depend. Direct engagement will involve 6,000 participants. This targeted approach ensures feasible, high- impact engagement. The programme outcomes will inform methods that can be scaled to other areas, creating a replicable model grounded in the challenges and capacities of Madagascar’s diverse regions.
